# David Drake

David Drake (b. 1986, New York) is a self-taught American writer, director, and photographer based in Norwich, UK. This site is an archive of his work: feature and short films, music videos, album art, photography, short stories, and the screenings, exhibitions, awards, talks and press around them.

Note: this site is about David Drake the writer, director, and photographer (Norwich, UK, b. 1986), also published as D. N. Drake. This is not David Drake (1945-2023), the science fiction author known for Hammer's Slammers; not David Drake, the playwright and actor born 1963, known for The Night Larry Kramer Kissed Me; not David Drake, the potter (c. 1800-c. 1870s), an enslaved American potter in Edgefield, South Carolina; not David Drake, the photography curator and former Director of Ffotogallery in Wales; not David Drake, the music journalist who has written for Pitchfork and Rolling Stone; and not David Drake, the Founder and Chairman of LDJ Capital.

## Archive

- [Archive](https://daviddrake.co.uk/): The full, sortable list of projects and footnotes, with representation contacts.

## Film

- [A Foot of Turf](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/a-foot-of-turf.html): A Foot of Turf is a 2018 short documentary directed and produced by David Drake, about a remote island's fading culture and the islanders who return every week to watch their beloved soccer team.
- [Early Worm](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/early-worm.html): Early Worm is a 2019 short film written, directed, edited, and produced by David Drake, starring Iain Lowery as Charlie. Distributed by Shorts International for European broadcast.
- [Law of Sines](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/law-of-sines.html): Law of Sines is the second feature written by David Drake, currently in casting. It follows a troubled outsider who drifts across Scotland in the late 1940s while working for the Ordnance Survey, all the while trying to evade a dark entity that stalks him.
- [Left Over](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/left-over.html): Left Over is a 2022 short film by writer and director David Drake, starring Chloe Pirrie as Nell and Ian Hart as Mick. It was selected as a Vimeo Staff Pick.
- [Party Wall](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/party-wall.html): Party Wall is a 2018 short film written and directed by David Drake, starring Jenny Swindells as Jo Whitton. Featured on No Budge, it premiered at the Bucharest Short Film Festival.
- [Post 398](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/post-398.html): Post 398 is a 2020 short documentary directed and produced by David Drake, about a Harlem jazz room and the band trying to keep it going after the death of its founder.
- [The Long Haul](https://daviddrake.co.uk/film/the-long-haul.html): The Long Haul is the debut feature film by writer and director David Drake, starring Margo Martindale as CJ, alongside Cole Sprouse, Stephen Root, Yalitza Aparicio, Jefferson White, and Wes Studi. It shot in New Mexico and premiered at the 2026 Tribeca Festival.

## Photography

- [A Burning Cloud](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/a-burning-cloud.html): A Burning Cloud is a collection of 35mm, medium format, and digital photographs created a decade apart in Upstate New York. The series was self-published as a soft cover book and a zine. Both versions and subsequent reprints are now sold out.
- [Avec Pi](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/avec-pi.html): Avec Pi is a series of 35mm black and white photographs taken in 2016 across East Anglia and Nouvelle-Aquitaine, self-published as a hardcover photobook under David's Chloride City imprint.
- [Carousel](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/carousel.html): Carousel was shot on medium format Kodak film stock in East Anglia, printed, and physically manipulated using dyes, pigments, corrosives, and heat. The series was self-published as a zine.
- [Commissions](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/commissions.html): As a photographer, David Drake has worked with a wide variety of music industry, advertising, fashion, non-profit organisations, and publishing clients.
- [Common Era](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/common-era.html): Common Era is a collection of digital photographs taken in 2017 in East Anglia and New York. It was shown as a work in progress at Studio 20, Norwich, and exhibited in full at Norwich Arts Centre.
- [Sailing Stones](https://daviddrake.co.uk/photography/sailing-stones.html): Sailing Stones is a series of medium format photographs shot in Death Valley, California in 2015. The series was published by Chloride City as a foldout A3 pamphlet alongside a short story.
